report.summary: Chunk 4 of daedalus/mapping/switches.py: defines functions for collecting env switches, reconciling defaults, and computing drift between documented and read env vars.
risks: _reconcile | medium | DARK requires unanimity on default plus at least one site with no fallback; logic uses `any(s.dark for s in real)` but doc says 'at least one site with no fallback' which is not directly checked. | Check if `s.dark` actually indicates no fallback or if additional check needed.
_drift | low | Near-miss pair detection uses token subsequence; may miss some near-misses or produce false positives for short names. | Review examples of near-misses to ensure correctness.
analyse | low | Uses `_augment_documented` to add bare mentions as documentation; may overcount if bare mention is not actual documentation. | Verify with specific doc files.

symbols.note: Main analysis function: scans sources, resolves defaults, computes drift.

claims.text: DARK requires unanimity on the default (every site reads it as off) plus at least one site with no fallback
claims.why: Code checks `states == {"OFF"} and any(s.dark for s in real)`. But `s.dark` is set in _collect_module? Not in this chunk. It doesn't check 'no fallback' directly; it checks `dark` attribute which may or may not mean no fallback.

claims.text: A variable that is off at one site and defaulted at another is MIXED, never dark
claims.why: Code sets `dark=False` if states != {'OFF'} (since condition requires states=={'OFF'}). So if any site is not OFF, dark is False.

claims.text: Two passes: every module is parsed before any default is resolved, so a default written as an imported constant is compared by VALUE.
claims.why: The chunk shows two passes but does not show how _Resolver resolves defaults. The claim about comparing by value is not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Names the code defines as module constants and never reads from the environment are dropped before drift is computed.
claims.why: Code: `for name in sorted(const_names - set(by_name)): documented.pop(name, None)` -- drops constant names not in by_name from documented.

claims.text: A near-miss pair is the silent bug: the operator sets the documented name and nothing happens.
claims.why: This is a general statement about the purpose; no code to verify.

claims.text: Only strict token-subsequence pairs qualify, so OLLAMA_NUM_CTX and OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL are not accused of being the same variable spelled two ways.
claims.why: Code checks `len(a) == len(b): continue` so same-length pairs are skipped. Also checks `short[0] != long[0]` and `_is_subsequence`. OLLAMA_NUM_CTX (3 tokens) and OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL (3 tokens) have same length, so they are skipped.

claims.text: docs/HANDOFF.md lists some variables as bare lines inside a fenced block, which matches no operator-shaped form.
claims.why: The claim refers to a specific file not in this chunk.

claims.text: Requiring the strict form there would manufacture a 'read but never documented' finding for a name the docs plainly show, and the whole point of the drift list is that every entry is worth acting on.
claims.why: Rationale not verifiable from code alone.

observations.what: _reconcile uses `any(s.dark for s in real)` but docstring says 'at least one site with no fallback'. The 'dark' attribute might not exactly represent 'no fallback'.
_config_switches reads JSON files from projects/*.json and *settings*.json, config.json. It uses `_read_text` and `_flatten` which are not defined in this chunk.
analyse function calls `_iter_sources`, `_collect_module`, `_Resolver`, `_scan_module`, `_iter_docs`, `_DOC_ENV_FORMS`, `_ENV_TOKEN`, `_PLATFORM_ENV`, `_tokens` which are not defined in this chunk.
_drift function uses `_tokens` which is not defined in this chunk.
The comment 'DARK requires unanimity ... plus at least one site with no fallback' may be inaccurate if `s.dark` does not represent 'no fallback'.
